CBSA.CICSBSA.ABNDFILE.recovery_why: etc/install/base/installjcl/BANK.csd: DEFINE FILE(ABNDFILE) ... RECOVERY(NONE) -- the abend log a backout must not undo

scenarios.name: current-found
scenarios.why: cursor OPEN +0, FETCH +0, CLOSE +0: every column moved, the three dates reformatted from Db2's ISO text into DDMMYYYY; available and actual balances differ; 'Y'

scenarios.name: saving-found
scenarios.why: type SAVING with an interest rate

scenarios.name: loan-negative-balance
scenarios.why: type LOAN: negative DECIMAL(12,2) balances into the signed S9(10)V99 COMMAREA fields

scenarios.name: mortgage-found
scenarios.why: type MORTGAGE, a large negative balance

scenarios.name: max-values-leap-day
scenarios.why: rate 9999.99, overdraft 99999999, available 9999999999.99 and actual -9999999999.99 (the largest each PICTURE holds); opened 2024-02-29

scenarios.name: overdraft-past-picture
scenarios.why: INTEGER overdraft 123456789 through S9(9) COMP into 9(8): the high-order digit is lost (23456789); statement dates across a year end

scenarios.name: negative-overdraft
scenarios.why: INTEGER overdraft -250 into the unsigned 9(8): the sign is dropped; a one-cent negative available balance

scenarios.name: account-zero
scenarios.why: boundary: account number 00000000 exists and is read through the cursor

scenarios.name: account-99999998
scenarios.why: boundary: the account just below the sentinel takes the cursor path

scenarios.name: last-account-sentinel
scenarios.why: INQACC-ACCNO 99999999: READ-ACCOUNT-LAST's SELECT ... ORDER BY ACCOUNT_NUMBER DESC FETCH FIRST 1 ROW gives the highest account of sort code 987654 (99999998), 'Y'

scenarios.name: not-found
scenarios.why: the cursor's FETCH +100 (no row): OUTPUT-DATA initialized, ACCOUNT-TYPE spaces, 'N'; the rest of the COMMAREA untouched

scenarios.name: other-sort-code-not-found
scenarios.why: account 00000010 exists only under sort code 123456; the cursor uses the program's own SORTCODE (987654), not INQACC-SCODE: +100, 'N'

scenarios.name: blank-account-type
scenarios.why: a row whose ACCOUNT_TYPE is all spaces: FETCH +0 but ACCOUNT-TYPE = SPACES, 'N'

scenarios.name: null-statement-date
scenarios.why: ACCOUNT_LAST_STATEMENT NULL with no indicator: FETCH -305; CHECK-FOR-STORM-DRAIN-DB2 (WHEN OTHER), ABNDINFO filled from the clock and EIB, LINK ABNDPROC (an ABNDFILE record), then ABEND HRAC CANCEL

scenarios.name: open-deadlock-abends-ad2z
scenarios.why: #6271 (X73): OPEN ACC-CURSOR deadlocks (-911) and the CICS-Db2 attach's syncpoint rollback fails: the task abends AD2Z, so ABEND-HANDLING takes its AD2Z arm (SQLERRMC the deadlock reason code 00C90088) and ABENDs

scenarios.name: fetch-deadlock-abends-ad2z
scenarios.why: #6271 (X73): the FETCH of ACC-CURSOR deadlocks (-911) and the attach's rollback fails: AD2Z, so ABEND-HANDLING takes its AD2Z arm

scenarios.name: open-connection-lost
scenarios.why: DB2 connection lost (SQLCODE 923) on OPEN: CHECK-FOR-STORM-DRAIN-DB2 sees WHEN 923 (Storm Drain condition met), ABNDINFO filled, LINK ABNDPROC, ABEND HRAC CANCEL

scenarios.name: cursor-close-fails
scenarios.why: CLOSE ACC-CURSOR refused (-501, cursor not open) after a good FETCH: the failure path after the CLOSE (CHECK-FOR-STORM-DRAIN-DB2 WHEN OTHER, ABNDINFO, LINK ABNDPROC, ABEND HRAC CANCEL)

scenarios.name: open-fails-link-abndproc-abends-afcr
scenarios.why: #6271 (X70): OPEN ACC-CURSOR (l.270) is refused -501, so the failure path LINKs ABNDPROC (l.321) and that LINK abends AFCR (an RLS file control abend seen at the caller): INQACC's own HANDLE ABEND exit takes the AFCR arm of ABEND-HANDLING (l.672-677, storm drain 'Y') and the SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK is NORMAL: the l.687 success arm, 'N' and RETURN

scenarios.name: open-fails-link-abndproc-abends-afcs
scenarios.why: #6271 (X70): OPEN ACC-CURSOR (l.270) is refused -501, so the failure path LINKs ABNDPROC (l.321) and that LINK abends AFCS (an RLS file control abend seen at the caller): INQACC's own HANDLE ABEND exit takes the AFCS arm of ABEND-HANDLING (l.672-677, storm drain 'Y') and the SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK is NORMAL: the l.687 success arm, 'N' and RETURN

scenarios.name: open-fails-link-abndproc-abends-afct
scenarios.why: #6271 (X70): OPEN ACC-CURSOR (l.270) is refused -501, so the failure path LINKs ABNDPROC (l.321) and that LINK abends AFCT (an RLS file control abend seen at the caller): INQACC's own HANDLE ABEND exit takes the AFCT arm of ABEND-HANDLING (l.672-677, storm drain 'Y') and the SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK is NORMAL: the l.687 success arm, 'N' and RETURN

scenarios.name: open-fails-link-abndproc-abends-afct-rollback-invreq
scenarios.why: #6271 (X70, X71): OPEN ACC-CURSOR (l.270) is refused -501, so the failure path LINKs ABNDPROC (l.321) and that LINK abends AFCT (an RLS file control abend seen at the caller): INQACC's own HANDLE ABEND exit takes the AFCT arm of ABEND-HANDLING (l.672-677, storm drain 'Y') and its SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK (l.682) answers INVREQ (RESP2 200): the l.687 failure arm

scenarios.name: open-attach-abends-ad2x
scenarios.why: #6271 (X73): OPEN ACC-CURSOR is issued and the CICS-Db2 attach's TCB fails (AD2X): the task abends AD2X, so ABEND-HANDLING takes its none arm (an abend code that is neither AD2Z nor a storm-drain AFC code) and ABENDs it afterwards

notes: CBSA's inquire-account service (INQACC, LINKed by BNK1DAC / BNK1UAC with the INQACC copybook's COMMAREA). INQACC-ACCNO 99999999 reads the highest account of the program's own sort code (987654) with SELECT ... ORDER BY ACCOUNT_NUMBER DESC FETCH FIRST 1 ROW; any other number OPENs cursor ACC-CURSOR on the program's SORTCODE (not INQACC-SCODE) and INQACC-ACCNO, FETCHes once and CLOSEs. FETCH +100 initializes the output; any other non-zero SQLCODE (e.g. -305, a NULL date with no indicator) fills ABNDINFO from the clock and EIB, LINKs ABNDPROC (run in the same task: an ABNDFILE record) and ABENDs HRAC CANCEL. An ACCOUNT-TYPE of spaces or low-values gives INQACC-SUCCESS 'N', else the COMMAREA is filled (dates reformatted from Db2's ISO text to DDMMYYYY) and 'Y'. ACCOUNT has a unique index on (sort code, number), so the cursor never has more than one row. Both ACCOUNT and ABNDFILE are compared after every scenario. abndfile.bin is empty (the file starts with no records).
